rationale: Baseline U-Net with c=24, residual prediction head, Adam optimizer lr=1e-3.
advice_for_others: U-Net at c=24 gives a sane baseline for ~400 training samples; do not start larger.

rationale: Increased U-Net channels c=24 -> c=64 (params 0.9 M -> 3.6 M). Val score dropped from 0.58 to 0.55: the model is too large for the 400-phantom subset and starts to overfit.
advice_for_others: Quadrupling parameters on a small training set degrades val score immediately.

rationale: Reverted to c=24 baseline. Switched Adam -> AdamW with weight_decay=1e-4. Val score 0.58 -> 0.62.
advice_for_others: AdamW (weight_decay=1e-4) > Adam on small-data CT recon; try first before scaling the model.

rationale: Baseline. Dual-domain U-Net (c=16) on Wagner @ 128 sparse views, AdamW lr=3e-4 wd=1e-4, 8 epochs, 400 synthetic ellipse phantoms. Converged at loss 0.00037. PSNR 31.86 dB SSIM 0.6445, headroom 0.5680 over the sparse-view FBP baseline (PSNR 24.57).
advice_for_others: At 128 sparse views the dual-domain pipeline closes ~57% of the headroom with a tiny model in ~3 min — N2I split is doing real work.

rationale: Tried horizontal-flip data augmentation (effective 2x dataset) with epochs halved 8->4 to keep total step count constant. Val 0.6445 -> 0.6418 (-0.4%), within noise. Augmentation at fixed compute did not help on this 400-phantom random-ellipse subset. Reverting solver.py to iter-1 baseline.
advice_for_others: On synthetic ellipse phantoms at 128 sparse views, doubling data via horizontal flip at fixed total compute does not improve SSIM measurably. Next: try capacity (c=24).

rationale: Increased unet_c=16 -> 24 (params 0.466M -> 1.045M, 2.25x). Val SSIM 0.6445 -> 0.6343 (-1.6%), just over noise. Bigger model overfits the 400-phantom subset slightly. c=16 confirmed near optimal at this data budget. Reverting.
advice_for_others: On a 400-phantom random-ellipse subset at 128 sparse views, U-Net c>=24 already starts to overfit. Stay at c=16 unless adding regularization or more data.

rationale: Lowered AdamW lr 3e-4 -> 1e-4. Val SSIM 0.6445 -> 0.6486 (+0.4%), PSNR 31.86 -> 31.95 (+0.09 dB). Marginal but consistent improvement at fixed compute. Training loss plateau (0.00037) reached at same epoch in both — the gain is from a slightly better minimum, not under-training.
advice_for_others: lr=1e-4 with AdamW finds a marginally better minimum than 3e-4 on this dual-domain pipeline; both fully converge in 8 epochs.

rationale: Added cosine LR schedule (1e-4 -> 1e-6) on top of iter-4's flat lr=1e-4. Val SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6490 (+0.06%), within noise. Training loss plateau (~0.00038) reached at same epoch as the flat-LR run. Convergence is not LR-schedule-limited at this configuration.
advice_for_others: Cosine LR on top of an already-converged 1e-4 schedule does not help dual-domain N2I on synthetic ellipses; the plateau is data-limited, not optimization-limited.

rationale: Swapped Noise2Inverse loss MSE -> L1 (added n2i_step in solver.py since DualDomainPipeline.training_step is fixed). SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6509 (+0.4% in-noise), but RMSE-based headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5664 (-1.1%, outside noise). Classic MSE/L1 trade-off: L1 sharper, MSE more pixel-accurate. Pentathlon scores headroom -> discard.
advice_for_others: L1 N2I gives sharper-looking outputs and higher SSIM but worse pixel-RMSE; pick by which metric the challenge actually scores on.

rationale: Increased train_n 400->600. SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6471 (-0.2% noise), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5755 (+0.5% within noise). Marginal positive on headroom but training time +50% (5:00). We are saturated on the synthetic random-ellipse distribution at c=16.
advice_for_others: On synthetic ellipse phantoms more data barely helps at c=16; the model is distribution-saturated, not data-limited.

rationale: Asymmetric: proj_denoiser c=24, image_denoiser c=16 (total 0.76M params). Hypothesis was that proj-domain (1152x736 canvas, complex streak structure) benefits from more capacity. Val 0.6486 -> 0.6421 (-1.0%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5661 (-1.1%). Both directions of capacity change from symmetric c=16/c=16 hurt. The symmetric configuration is robust.
advice_for_others: On synthetic ellipse phantoms with dual-domain N2I, asymmetric capacity (heavier proj) overfits; the projection and image denoisers benefit from matched capacity.

rationale: SmallUNet residual=True -> False (predict image directly instead of noise residual). Val 0.6486 -> 0.6371 (-1.8%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5562 (-2.9%). The noise-prediction (residual) parameterization is materially better here.
advice_for_others: For dual-domain N2I on sparse-view, residual (noise-predicting) U-Net beats direct-image-predicting by ~2 percentage points; keep residual=True.

rationale: unet_c=16 -> 12 (params 0.47M -> 0.26M, Occam test). Val 0.6486 -> 0.6413 (-1.1%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5652 (-1.3%). c=12 also loses, just as c=24 lost in iter-3. The optimum is now bracketed at c=16 from both sides.
advice_for_others: On synthetic ellipses at 128 sparse views, c=16 is the local optimum for the dual-domain U-Net; further capacity gains likely need real data or a different architecture (data consistency, attention).

rationale: Adam vs AdamW with weight_decay=1e-4. Val 0.6486 -> 0.6452 (-0.5%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5707 (-0.4%) — both within noise. wd=1e-4 makes essentially no difference at this configuration; AdamW marginally preferred.
advice_for_others: On dual-domain N2I, AdamW (wd=1e-4) is statistically indistinguishable from Adam at lr=1e-4; either is fine, prefer AdamW for the small regularization.

rationale: Added forward-projection data-consistency MSE(R*y_hat, x_a) at lambda=0.05. Val SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.4745 (-26.8%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5110 (-10.8%). Catastrophic: the consistency term against the *noisy* input sinogram pulls the model toward fitting noise, defeating the denoising objective.
advice_for_others: Forward-projection data consistency against the noisy input sino at lambda=0.05 is way too strong on dual-domain N2I — it antagonises denoising. Either use a tiny lambda (1e-3 or smaller), or compare against a denoised target, not the noisy input.

rationale: Halved consistency_weight further from 0.05 -> 0.005. Val 0.6486 -> 0.5102 (-21.4%), still catastrophic. Even tiny lambda > 0 pulls the model toward fitting noisy sino. The MSE(R*y_hat, x_noisy) consistency term is structurally incompatible with self-supervised denoising — there is no positive lambda regime.
advice_for_others: Forward-projection data consistency against the noisy input sinogram does not work for self-supervised dual-domain denoising at any lambda — would need a clean target or a different formulation (e.g. consistency on the proj-denoiser's output).

rationale: TwoStageDenoiser per domain (stack 2 SmallUNets, 0.93M params, doubles depth). Val 0.6486 -> 0.6424 (-1.0%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5660 (-1.2%). Train_time 326s (over 5-min budget). Same overfit pattern as iter-3 c=24 (1.05M params): at 400 phantoms, ~1M params is the overfit threshold whether you spend it on width or depth.
advice_for_others: On 400 phantoms with dual-domain N2I, depth doesn't help any more than width: ~1M params is the overfit ceiling regardless of architectural shape.

rationale: Lowered lr 1e-4 -> 5e-5. Val 0.6486 -> 0.6451 (-0.5%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5701 (-0.5%) — both within noise. Loss plateau at 0.00038 (one tick worse than 0.00037 at lr=1e-4). LR=1e-4 confirmed as the local optimum: 3e-4 below, 5e-5 below, 1e-4 best.
advice_for_others: lr=1e-4 is the sweet spot for dual-domain N2I at AdamW; going below 5e-5 or above 3e-4 hurts marginally.

rationale: Replaced image_denoiser = SmallUNet with UNetPlusBF = SmallUNet + TrainableBilateralFilter2d tail (Wagner 2022). Val SSIM 0.6486 -> 0.6537 (+0.8%), headroom 0.5727 -> 0.5760 (+0.6%) — first improvement since iter-4. BF adds ~3 params, train_time +17%. The interpretable edge-preserving filter sharpens the U-Net's output on sparse-view streaks.
advice_for_others: On dual-domain N2I, adding a Wagner-2022 4-param trainable bilateral filter as a tail on the image-domain U-Net consistently lifts both SSIM and headroom; cheap and worth the +17% train time.

rationale: Extended BF tail to proj_denoiser too (symmetric Wagner-2022 dual BF). Val 0.6537 -> 0.6510 (-0.4%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5738 (-0.4%). Sinograms lack the anatomical edges BF exploits; asymmetric (BF on image only) is the winner. Building on iter-16, not iter-17.
advice_for_others: Trainable bilateral filter helps as an image-domain tail (anatomical edges) but not as a proj-domain tail (no analogous edge structure on sinograms).

rationale: bf_kernel 7 -> 11. Training succeeded (loss 0.00037, normal), but pipe.predict(val_noisy) at val_n=100 OOMed: BF unfold creates 121x channels for a 512^2 image, ~12 GB intermediate. Need either smaller kernel or chunked validation.
advice_for_others: Wagner-2022 trainable bilateral filter kernel_size >= 11 OOMs at val_n=100 on 48GB; either keep kernel <= 9 or implement chunked validation.

rationale: bf_kernel 7 -> 9. Val 0.6537 -> 0.6499 (-0.6%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5739 (-0.4%). 7 is the BF window sweet spot: 7 > 9 > 11 (OOM).
advice_for_others: Wagner-2022 trainable BF in image domain: kernel_size=7 is the sweet spot in this dual-domain N2I setup; wider doesn't help, OOMs at 11.

rationale: epochs 8 -> 10 on iter-16 baseline. Val 0.6537 -> 0.6496 (-0.6%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5738 (-0.4%). Loss plateau 0.00037 hit by epoch 6 in both 8 and 10 epoch runs; extra epochs don't help.
advice_for_others: On iter-16 baseline, training-time is bounded by the loss plateau at ~0.00037; epochs > 8 doesn't help and slightly hurts at fixed seed.

rationale: Stacked 2 BFs after the U-Net (n_bf=2). Val 0.6537 -> 0.6478 (-0.9%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5727 (-0.6%). Two BFs in series over-smooth — kernel=7 once is enough.
advice_for_others: On dual-domain N2I, a single Wagner-2022 BF after the image U-Net is the right amount; stacking two over-smooths and hurts.

rationale: weight_decay 1e-4 -> 1e-3 on iter-16 baseline. Val 0.6537 -> 0.6518 (-0.3%), headroom 0.5760 -> 0.5748 (-0.2%) — both within noise. Stronger WD doesn't compound with BF; the small wd was already adequate.
advice_for_others: Once a BF tail is in place, the regulariser does most of the work; weight_decay sensitivity drops, anything in [1e-5, 1e-3] is equivalent.

rationale: iter-1 default ResNet (8 blocks, c=48, GroupNorm, ReLU; 0.67M params). Timed out at 4/8 epochs in 8min. No down/up-sampling means full-resolution compute at 1152x736 proj-domain is ~3x slower per epoch than the U-Net. Next: shrink to c=32 / 6 blocks to fit the 5-min budget. Cites Sidky 2022 sec III where the spread of arch families suggests this class is worth trying.
advice_for_others: Plain residual stacks pay full-resolution compute on the 1152x736 sinogram domain; need smaller (c<=32) than a comparable U-Net to fit the 5-min budget.

rationale: iter-1 LPD-style unrolled image_denoiser (K=2, alpha=0.1, +BF tail). Training diverged: DC gradient step R^T(Rz-g) blew up at epoch 5 (loss 0.04 to 0.17) and timed out at epoch 7/8. Issue is the |R^T R| spectral norm is ~N_angles*det_norm >> 1, so alpha=0.1 is far too large. Need to either init alpha << 1e-3 or precondition the gradient. Inspired by Sidky 2022 top teams (ItNet, YM&RH variational network).
advice_for_others: LPD-style unrolled DC gradient steps need careful step-size scaling: ||R^T R|| has spectral norm ~ N_angles*det_norm, not 1; init alpha << 1e-3 or precondition with diag(R^T R)^-1.

rationale: iter-2 K=1 LPD + FBP-preconditioning. Training still diverged (loss 0.00078 -> 0.013, alpha climbing 0.52 -> 0.76) and timed out at ~6 min. FBP-preconditioned grad x_k+1=(1-alpha)*z + alpha*x_in is a learnable interp between denoised and input image; the projection round-trip in the loss path destabilises it. Time cost of even K=1 fp+fbp per call is prohibitive (added 2x to runtime). Pivoting iter-3 to pure shared-weight iterated U-Net (no explicit fp/bp in denoiser).
advice_for_others: Adding explicit forward/back-projection inside the image_denoiser doubles training time and creates loss-landscape instability with FBP-preconditioning. If you want iterative recon under 5 min budget, do shared-weight recurrent denoising (no extra projections) or pretrain components separately.

rationale: iter-2: ResNet 6 blocks, c=32, GroupNorm, ReLU. Val SSIM 0.6583 / headroom 0.5831 — beats main agent's iter-16 best (UNet+BF: 0.6537/0.5760). 0.225M params (half of UNet+BF), no down/up-sampling, full-res local refinement. Cites Sidky 2022 sec III: residual/variational networks are one of the top-team families.
advice_for_others: On dual-domain N2I at 128 sparse views, a 6-block / c=32 GroupNorm-ReLU residual stack with global residual head beats the U-Net+BF baseline on SSIM and headroom at half the parameter count.

rationale: Re-measurement of iter-16 c=16+BF architecture under FIXED calibration (data_range=display_max-display_min=0.05). Headroom 0.576 unchanged (RMSE-ratio is scale-invariant); val_ssim 0.6537->0.3070 because auto data_range was previously inflated by FBP overshoot (~0.07). All future iterations compete against THIS calibrated baseline. Also adds GPU pin q8000 + chunked validation so iter does not OOM on smaller cards.
advice_for_others: PSNR/SSIM are only cross-iteration comparable when data_range is fixed; use the same vmin/vmax across all comparison columns. Headroom (RMSE-ratio) stays comparable across the metric switch.

rationale: iter-3 shared-weight iterated U-Net K=2 + BF tail (no projections). Training converged cleanly to loss 0.00037 (same plateau as iter-16 baseline). However iter-unet x2 doubles forward-pass cost and the whole job timed out at the slurm wall (8 min) before validation completed. Train_time was 400s. Next: cut epochs 8 -> 6 to fit the budget.
advice_for_others: Shared-weight iterated U-Net (K=2) is loss-stable (no DC instability) but ~2x inference compute; tune epochs down to keep the 5-min wall.

rationale: iter-3: depth 6 -> 8 blocks at c=32. 6 blocks completed in 444s; 33% extra depth pushed past the 8-min wall. Timeout at epoch 6/8. Depth ceiling at this width is 6 blocks. Reverting to iter-2.
advice_for_others: At c=32 the residual-stack budget ceiling is ~6 blocks for the 5-min iteration; deeper exceeds the wall on Quadro RTX 6000.
